title: Choose the visual world for Violation Ticketing
question: The roll assigned the License Plate world. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: License Plate
options.lineage: LTO plates and plate-class colours every Filipino reads at a glance
options.thesis: Every Control Number is shown as a plate: big, embossed, condensed, readable from arm's length in full sun.
options.viewport: Phone Home: slim asphalt top bar with Citation Type tabs, the current Control Number as a full-width plate, a forms-left tally strip under it, one big Start citation button, Today list below.
options.risk: Plate framing everywhere turns into a gimmick; it has to stay on numbers only.

raised.raise: One type family carries every level, from the plate numerals to the captions; tables are built from 1px rules, not boxed cards.
Enforcer Home is a single-object screen: the plate and Start citation own the first view, nothing competes in the centre.
A Booklet has a fixed capacity, drawn as a strip of one cell per form that fills as forms are Done, Cancelled or Voided.
Night is designed, not inverted: asphalt shell, plate stays bright like a retroreflective plate under headlights.
Neutrals come from one fixed ramp only; state colours are the plate classes: green Done, red Voided, yellow Not synced.

options.label: Carbonless Booklet
options.thesis: The screen is the top copy of the form: red numbering-machine serials, white, pink and canary copies as state colours.
options.viewport: Phone Home: white sheet, the Control Number in red numbering-machine digits top right as on the paper, form-style ruled boxes, Start citation at the bottom.
options.risk: The most literal reading of the brief and what most runs would land on; can feel like paperwork on a screen.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: Registration crosshairs and hairlines on near-white stock, one grotesque throughout.
options.viewport: Citation list as plates on a sheet with crosshair corners.
options.case: Enforcers and Treasury staff don't know this world; crosshairs add ornament, not clarity.
options.risk: Reads as a portfolio, not a working tool.
options.kept: One family carries every level; rules, not boxes, build the tables.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One Control Number owns the screen, the next one a snap away.
options.viewport: Each form a full screen; swipe to the next number.
options.case: Familiar, but it supplies the navigation model, and swiping past numbers contradicts strict order.
options.risk: Invites skipping forms with a flick.

options.label: Cassette J-card
options.thesis: Two sides that must not overflow the tape.
options.case: No connection to field enforcement; handwriting hurts sunlight legibility.
options.kept: Fixed capacity: the Booklet as a strip that fills.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Hierarchy by dot size on a navy chart, red night light.
options.viewport: Citations plotted as stars by day.
options.case: Beautiful but unrelated to the job; a navy ground fails in direct sun.
options.kept: A night mode designed for night use.

options.label: Exposure Zone Sheets
options.thesis: Translucent sheets over an eleven-step zone ramp; hatching marks load and conflict.
options.case: Nobody in the audience reads darkroom notation; hatching is hard to read on a phone in sun.
options.kept: One fixed neutral ramp; colour only for state.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A government field-app done well: white cards, blue primary, Material-style controls.
canonCard.viewport: Blue app bar, a card with the current number, a blue Start button, a bottom tab bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other government app by design.
